Write a standard reduction kernel with grid-stride within block: each thread loads elements with stride blockDim.x, guarding bounds, accumulates into local sum, then shared reduction tree with all threads participating.

Simple approach: load sdata[tid] = (i < n) ? in[i] : 0 with i = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + tid, then reduce. But that only handles one element per thread — fine since blocks = ceil(n/threads), each element covered exactly once. That satisfies contract. But better to do strided loop? With blocks = ceil(n/threads), each thread has exactly one element. Simple one-element-per-thread is correct.

Reduction: for (s = blockDim.x/2; s > 0; s >>= 1) { if (tid < s) sdata[tid] += sdata[tid+s]; __syncthreads(); } — all threads reach syncthreads since the barrier is outside the if. Then thread 0 writes out.
